claim: Customs cash was the dominant usable federal revenue supporting debt service during 1789–1803.
mechanism: Imported cargo generated assessed duties; collection converted obligations into Treasury cash.
required_evidence: Reconciled Treasury receipts; customs assessments; bonds; cash collection; debt-service accounts
counterfactual_or_comparison: Other revenue sources and periods of weak customs realization
contradicting_evidence: Customs cash is minor after consistent accounting or is unavailable when debt service falls due

claim: Credit terms, customs bonds, and drawbacks linked trade policy to merchant working capital and re-export activity.
mechanism: Deferred duties and drawback timing altered capital tied up between entry, sale, and re-export.
required_evidence: Entries; bonds; maturities; payments/defaults; drawback claims and payments; ledgers or correspondence
counterfactual_or_comparison: Cash-duty transactions; merchants without re-export; variation across rule changes
contradicting_evidence: Timing or access to customs credit has no observable relation to financing or re-export decisions

claim: Reliable debt service improved the marketability of United States obligations at home and in Europe.
mechanism: Observed payment performance reduced perceived default and transfer risk; intermediaries placed and serviced securities.
required_evidence: Debt-service accounts; security prices/yields; transfers; correspondence; commissions; exchange rates
counterfactual_or_comparison: Other sovereign securities; shocks unrelated to U.S. fiscal performance
contradicting_evidence: Prices or placement deteriorate despite reliable service, or move only with common European factors

claim: The First Bank functioned as an operating link in Treasury payments and commercial credit, not merely as a statutory design.
mechanism: Deposits, transfers, discounts, notes, and branch operations connected public balances and private payments.
unit_of_analysis: bank unit or transaction x date
required_evidence: Bank/Treasury correspondence; ledgers; branch records; discounts; balances; transfers
counterfactual_or_comparison: Ports or periods without comparable Bank access
contradicting_evidence: No observed operational link between Bank activity, Treasury flows, or merchant finance

claim: The Louisiana Purchase financing used demonstrated federal debt capacity and European intermediation without interrupting existing debt service.
mechanism: Congressional authorization and new obligations were converted through intermediaries into settlement value while existing obligations continued.
unit_of_analysis: purchase obligation or payment x date
required_evidence: Authorization; claims convention; stock issue; contracts; Baring/Hope records; proceeds; fees; exchange; Treasury debt service
counterfactual_or_comparison: Contemporaneous financing alternatives and existing capacity constraints
contradicting_evidence: Purchase obligations cannot be reconciled, required extraordinary revenue interruption, or were independent of prior credit performance

claim: Replacing treaty-dependent access with a U.S. sovereignty claim changed political risk around the Mississippi–New Orleans corridor.
mechanism: Ownership claim altered the legal and diplomatic source of access uncertainty but did not itself create commerce or prove lower route costs.
required_evidence: Treaties; deposit chronology; diplomatic correspondence; route costs; shipment evidence; seizures or interruptions
counterfactual_or_comparison: Pre/post access conditions; alternative Atlantic routes; unresolved boundaries and effective control
contradicting_evidence: Commercial use or route costs do not change, or other constraints dominate after transfer

claim: The fiscal-commercial system distributed benefits, taxes, finance, and losses unevenly across regions and actors.
mechanism: Port concentration, credit access, enslaved production, and exposure to shocks allocated gains and burdens unequally.
unit_of_analysis: port, merchant, producer, or selected household x period
required_evidence: Merchant samples; prices/wages for bounded cases; production records; tax incidence; defaults; seizures
counterfactual_or_comparison: Variation across ports, merchant access, commodity systems, and free versus enslaved labor
contradicting_evidence: Available microevidence shows no meaningful concentration or systematic distributional difference
